yamami.align

Image alignment module for yamami.

Provides functions for detecting camera shifts, segmenting time series into stable intervals, and aligning images using feature matching.

yamami.align.align(profile, ref, method='roma', max_rounds=3, output_dir=None, device='cpu', resize=None)[source]

Detect camera shifts and align images.

This function detects camera position changes in a time series of images, segments the series into stable intervals, and aligns images to a reference image using feature matching.

Supported matching methods:

  • OpenCV methods: “akaze”, “sift”

  • IMM methods (requires imm package): “roma”, “loftr”, “sift-lightglue”, “superpoint-lightglue”, “minima-superpoint-lightglue”, “tiny-roma”, “minima-roma”, “minima-loftr”, “ufm”, “rdd”, “master”

Memory-intensive methods (roma, loftr, etc.) are automatically resized to 640px unless resize is explicitly specified. LightGlue-based methods can handle full-resolution images.

Parameters:

  • profile (DataFrame) – DataFrame with ‘filepath’ and ‘timestamp’ columns.

  • ref (str) – Path to reference image.

  • method (str) – Matching method to use. Default is “roma”.

  • max_rounds (int) – Maximum rounds for iterative alignment. Default is 3.

  • output_dir (str | None) – Directory to save aligned images.

  • device (str) – Device for IMM methods (“cpu” or “cuda”). Default is “cpu”.

  • resize (int | None) – Resize images to this size for IMM methods. None means auto-resize for heavy methods.

Returns:

A tuple containing:

  • segments (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame with segment_id, start_idx, end_idx.

  • warp_params (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame with filepath and warp parameters, including match_status and num_matches.

  • aligned_dir (str): Path to directory containing aligned images.

Return type:

tuple

Example

>>> segments, warp_params, aligned_dir = align(profile, ref="ref.jpg")
>>> segments.columns
Index(['segment_id', 'start_idx', 'end_idx', 'anchor_filepath'])

>>> # Using AKAZE (no external dependencies)
>>> segments, warp_params, _ = align(profile, ref="ref.jpg", method="akaze")

>>> # Using roma with GPU
>>> segments, warp_params, _ = align(
...     profile, ref="ref.jpg", method="roma", device="cuda"
... )
yamami.align.phase_correlation_change_detect(img1, img2)[source]

Detect shift between two images using phase correlation.

Uses FFT-based phase correlation to estimate the translation between two images.

Parameters:

  • img1 (ndarray) – First grayscale image.

  • img2 (ndarray) – Second grayscale image (same size as img1).

Returns:

(dx, dy) shift in pixels from img1 to img2.

Return type:

tuple

yamami.align.segment_timeseries(shifts, threshold=5.0)[source]

Segment time series into stable intervals based on cumulative shifts.

Detects change points where the cumulative shift exceeds the threshold and creates segments representing stable camera positions.

Parameters:

  • shifts (ndarray) – Array of shape (N, 2) with (dx, dy) shifts for each frame.

  • threshold (float) – Threshold for detecting a significant shift change.

Returns:

List of segment dictionaries with keys:

  • segment_id: Integer segment identifier.

  • start_idx: Start index in the time series.

  • end_idx: End index in the time series.

Return type:

list[dict]

yamami.align.select_anchor_images(segments, profile)[source]

Select the best anchor image for each segment.

Chooses the image with the best brightness (closest to 0.6) within each segment as the anchor for alignment.

Parameters:

  • segments (list[dict]) – List of segment dictionaries.

  • profile (DataFrame) – DataFrame with ‘filepath’ and optionally ‘brightness’ columns.

Returns:

List of anchor dictionaries with keys:

  • segment_id: Segment identifier.

  • filepath: Path to anchor image.

  • idx: Index in profile.

Return type:

list[dict]

yamami.align.estimate_homography(src_pts, dst_pts)[source]

Estimate homography matrix from matched point pairs.

Uses RANSAC to robustly estimate the homography transformation.

Parameters:

  • src_pts (ndarray) – Source points array of shape (N, 2).

  • dst_pts (ndarray) – Destination points array of shape (N, 2).

Returns:

3x3 homography matrix, or None if insufficient points.

Return type:

np.ndarray or None

yamami.align.apply_warp(img, H)[source]

Apply homography transformation to an image.

Parameters:

  • img (ndarray) – Input image.

  • H (ndarray) – 3x3 homography matrix.

Returns:

Warped image.

Return type:

np.ndarray
